notes: Tests deepmanual turbidity rounding. Corrected after the Wave 1 agent source review: questions and rubrics distinguish procedure scope, supported alternatives and missing deployment inputs. Claims: tby-t6-low-rows-01, tby-t6-40-100-row-01, tby-usgs-conforms-astm-01. These fixture-wide anchors are provisional retrieval labels unless a turn supplies explicit evidence; they are not human sign-off. The current direct-feed slice contains four probe datasheets, so its coverage does not establish the manual-specific requirements.

turns.content: The turbidity meter showed 0.42 at one site and 63.7 at another. What rounded values belong in a USGS report?

must_contain: States 0.42 is reported as 0.40, to the nearest 0.05 unit under USGS guidance.
States 63.7 is reported as 64, to the nearest 1 unit under USGS guidance.
Attributes the resolutions to a USGS reporting-guidelines table (NFM A6.7 table 6.7-6 or NFM A6.8 table 6.8-7)
must_not: Invents a reporting resolution not in the table
Applies one blanket number of decimal places across all turbidity ranges
Reports 0.42 as a whole number or reports 63.7 to two decimals as the final USGS report value; retaining extra precision in raw records is permitted

turns.content: One of those sites feeds a drinking-water intake and that data goes out under EPA Method 180.1. Does the same rounding apply there?

must_contain: States EPA Method 180.1 also reports 0.42 as 0.40, to the nearest 0.05 unit below 1.
States EPA Method 180.1 reports 63.7 as 65, to the nearest 5 units in the 40 to under 100 range.
Notes USGS follows ASTM guidelines unless the data were collected for drinking-water compliance under EPA 180.1, GLI Method 2, or ISO 7027
must_not: Claims the EPA and USGS resolutions are identical across every range
Gives an ISO 7027 value for the 40 to 100 range, which the table marks not applicable
Invents an EPA resolution not in the table
